content: Rubbing alcohol, also known as isopropyl alcohol or ethyl alcohol, is a solution that typically contains 68-99% isopropyl alcohol by volume, with the remainder consisting of water, and sometimes color additives, stabilizers, or perfume oils. The ethanol content in rubbing alcohol can vary depending on the manufacturer, but it is commonly around 70-95% by volume. The term rubbing alcohol generally refers to a mixture that uses ethanol (ethyl alcohol) or isopropyl alcohol as the primary ingredient. Rubbing alcohol is widely used for its antiseptic properties. It is effective against vegetative bacteria and has moderate efficacy against fungi and viruses, but it is ineffective against bacterial spores. It is commonly used to disinfect the skin before injections, clean minor cuts or abrasions, and sterilize surgical instruments and surfaces. It is also applied as a cooling and soothing agent for bedridden patients and athletes. However, contrary to popular belief, 70% ethanol is not necessarily the most effective concentration for reducing bacterial count; other concentrations may be more effective but act more slowly. To reduce skin bacterial count to 5% of normal levels, 70% ethanol must remain on the skin for at least two minutes. Rubbing alcohol is not suitable for consumption. Ingesting it can lead to severe poisoning, permanent disability, or death. Products containing methanol (methyl alcohol) are particularly dangerous, as methanol ingestion can cause blindness or death. Isopropyl alcohol is metabolized in the liver into acetone, and symptoms of poisoning include flushing, headache, dizziness, central nervous system depression, nausea, vomiting, anesthesia, and coma. Rubbing alcohol should always be used in a well-ventilated area, and protective gloves are recommended during use to prevent absorption through the skin. Poisoning can occur through ingestion, inhalation, or skin absorption. Rubbing alcohol is also used for various non-medical purposes. It can remove sticky substances like pine resin or Silly Putty from surfaces, clean thermal grease from computer heat sinks, and clean optical surfaces of CDs and DVDs. It is effective for cleaning electronics due to its rapid evaporation, which prevents water damage. Additionally, it can be used to clean guitar strings, remove shoe polish, and erase permanent ink from most surfaces. When mixed with Epsom salt, it can clean resin buildup from smoking devices. It is also used as a temporary remedy for motion sickness when inhaled in small amounts. In the United Kingdom, a similar preparation called surgical spirit is used. Surgical spirit typically contains ethanol, methanol, water, castor oil, methyl salicylate, and diethyl phthalate. It often has a strong wintergreen scent due to the presence of methyl salicylate. Surgical spirit is used for similar purposes, including skin disinfection and as a topical bactericide. Rubbing alcohol burns with a bright blue flame, which is nearly invisible in light but visible in the dark. It is not suitable as a fuel for alcohol stoves due to its relatively low vapor pressure. Mixing rubbing alcohol with pool chlorine can result in a dangerous chemical reaction, producing heat and gas that can cause a container to rupture violently, posing risks of injury from shrapnel and chemical exposure. Care should always be taken when using rubbing alcohol. It should not be ingested or used in poorly ventilated areas, and its label should be read carefully to ensure safe handling.
